title: Perfect Investigation
verdict: Every lie on the record, answered by an exhibit.
narrative: You take {accused}'s statement apart one line at a time, and every line has an exhibit waiting for it. The defence reads your file on Monday morning and asks for a plea by Monday afternoon.
The Argus-7 turns up on Tuesday in a rented lock-up off Route 9, still in its foam wrap, never switched on.
The District Attorney calls it the cleanest file her office has seen all year. Nobody at Halden Dynamics ever quite looks at a keycard the same way again.

title: True Criminal
verdict: The right name, and enough to hold it.
narrative: {accused} is charged on Monday morning, a few hours before the demonstration that never happens.
The case holds. The defence finds a few loose threads in court — questions you never asked, statements you never tested — but not enough to pull.
The Argus-7 is recovered in the spring. Somewhere in the file, a few lies were never answered. You keep it in your bottom drawer anyway.

title: Wrong Suspect
verdict: A careful case, built around the wrong person.
narrative: Your case against {accused} is careful. It places them, it tests their story, it holds up in the squad room. It is also wrong.
The charges fall apart before trial. By then, whoever really walked out of Halden that night has had months to cover their tracks.
In the autumn a prototype very like the Argus-7 appears in a competitor's catalogue. The file is reopened, and handed to somebody else.

title: Innocent Person Accused
verdict: An accusation with almost nothing behind it.
narrative: {accused} is arrested on a Monday morning with the evidence you had, which was not much.
The charges are dropped within the week. The damage isn't. The newspapers ran the name; they never ran the apology.
The Argus-7 is never recovered. The file is closed without a culprit, and yours is the name on the cover.

title: Criminal Escapes
verdict: The file never became a case.
narrative: The file goes to the District Attorney's office and comes back stamped INSUFFICIENT.
Whoever took the Argus-7 knew exactly how thin that file would be. The demonstration on Monday is cancelled. The sale falls through by summer.
Case #047 is shelved in a basement archive at Ridgeway, beside a great many others.
